questions: What is the exact definition of "splitting A at one position into subarrays" - does it mean choosing exactly one index i where 1 ≤ i ≤ N-1 to split into two non-empty parts?
Can the split occur at position 0 or position N, resulting in one empty subarray and one complete array?
When counting distinct integers in a subarray, does this refer to the number of unique values present in that subarray?
What should be the output when N = 2 - is there only one valid split position?
Are duplicate values in the sequence handled correctly when counting distinct elements?
Is the constraint "1 ≤ A_i ≤ N" strict or can A_i equal 0 or exceed N?
What is the expected behavior when all elements in the array are identical?
Should the solution consider integer overflow when summing the counts of distinct integers?

inline_prompts:
This problem is a simplified version of Problem F.  
You are given an integer sequence of length N: A = (A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_N).  
When splitting A at one position into subarrays, find the maximum possible sum of the counts of distinct integers in those subarrays.  
More formally, find the maximum sum of the following two values: the count of distinct integers in (A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_i), and the count of distinct integers in (A_{i+1}, A_{i+2}, \ldots, A_N).  
They must be contiguous and non-empty subarrays obtained by splitting A at one position.  
Input  
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:  
N  
A_1 A_2 \ldots A_N  
Output  
Print the answer.  
Constraints  
- 2 \leq N \leq 3 \times 10^5  
- 1 \leq A_i \leq N (1 \leq i \leq N)  
- All input values are integers.
